course.learning_goal: Explain why collaboration is important in computer science projects, describe how teams use shared roles, communication, version control, and feedback cycles to develop computing artifacts, and teach learners how to evaluate whether collaboration improves the quality, inclusiveness, and reliability of a project.
key_learning_points: Collaboration roles such as designer, developer, tester, and reviewer
Communication protocols for coordinating work and resolving disagreements
Version control and shared documents for tracking changes
Iterative feedback cycles including peer review and testing
Benefits and risks of collaboration, including diverse perspectives, coordination overhead, and accountability

student_persona:
Grade: High School AP Computer Science Principles
Focus Time: 15 minutes
Background Knowledge: Has: Basic experience working on school group projects and using shared online documents. Lacks: Formal understanding of software team roles, version control, peer review workflows, and how collaboration affects computing artifact quality.
